messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER TRIGGERED — High 5xx rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (start 2026-03-15T14:00:00Z)
Alice Chen: paging oncall, seeing spike from 14:00 UTC. ~25% errors, clients report timeouts.
Emma Rodriguez: I'm oncall, joining now. Can someone dump router logs & model node metrics?
Bob Singh: adding router tail:
```
[14:01:58] router-1 us-west-2 - upstream request -> model-12 timeout after 30s (504)
[14:02:03] router-2 us-west-2 - error EOF reading from model-12
[14:02:05] router-1 us-west-2 - connection reset by peer
```
Maya Patel: attaching edge LB stats: sudden spike in queued requests to the model pool, CPU on model-12 nodes low, GPU mem at ~80%.
Lucas Nguyen: interesting — low CPU but queued requests suggests blocked I/O or KV-cache stall. Any recent runtime or kernel changes?
Jason Li: last infra deploy was 2026-03-15T13:58 — runtime patch to async KV fetch (PR #4821).
Emma Rodriguez: hypothesis A: recent async KV change caused a deadlock under heavy concurrent prefixes -> requests pile up and time out.
Alice Chen: hypothesis B: autoscaler mis-scheduled shards after deploy -> overloaded subset of model nodes.
Bob Singh: I can run a quick `kubectl get pods -o wide` across model-12 pool and check pod restarts / OOMs.
Bob Singh: `kubectl exec` shows no OOMs, restart count 0. PVCs OK.
Maya Patel: I see a subset of model-12 replicas with higher network retransmits (netstat counters). Could be a NIC driver issue after kernel bump on the nodes.
Emma Rodriguez: ok we have three plausible hypotheses: async KV deadlock (Emma), mis-scheduled shards (Alice), NIC/kernel regression (Maya). Let's track tests and owners inline.
Emma Rodriguez: I'm owner for hypothesis: async KV deadlock. Test: revert runtime async KV change on one canary rack (rack-a) and see if errors drop. ETA 15m.
Alice Chen: I'm owner for hypothesis: shard mis-schedule. Test: check replica distribution and force a rebalance on one node. Command: `rctl model rebalance model-12 --node node-xyz --dry-run` then apply if safe. ETA 10m.
Maya Patel: I'm owner for hypothesis: NIC/kernel regression. Test: check kernel version across failing nodes and roll back kernel on a single node to previous AMI. ETA 25m.
Deploy Bot: deploy event detected: runtime/kv-async v2.3 deployed at 2026-03-15T13:58 by jason.li.
Jason Li: confirming I merged that PR; it was supposed to reduce tail latency by background fetching. Rolling back if needed.
Emma Rodriguez: starting canary revert now on rack-a: `helm rollback runtime 1 --namespace inference-rack-a`
Alice Chen: running rebalance dry-run, distribution shows 60% of traffic hitting node-xy1. Applying rebalance to move two replicas off.
Bob Singh: collecting aggregated logs for timeline: attaching paste (truncated):
```
14:00:55 router-1 5xx spike begins
14:01:30 high queue depth on model-12 pool
14:02:10 first observed connection reset to model-12
14:04:00 errors spread to second availability zone
14:09:20 mitigations started (rebalance + canary revert)
```
Maya Patel: kernel versions: failing nodes on us-west-2-a are kernel 6.2.1-custom, earlier nodes 6.1.8. The 6.2.1 kernel was part of a routine image refresh at 2026-03-15T12:40.
Emma Rodriguez: canary revert completed on rack-a at 14:10 UTC. Monitoring...
Alice Chen: rebalance applied at 14:11, two replicas moved off node-xy1.
Jason Li: rolling revert of runtime KV patch on one additional rack (rack-b) to be safe; logging this in the deploy pipeline.
Bob Singh: metrics: error rate on /v1/generate dropped from 25% -> 6% in rack-a by 14:14. Global error rate down to 12% by 14:16.
Maya Patel: after kernel rollback on node-xy1 (14:18), we see network retransmits drop and queued depth reduced.
Emma Rodriguez: preliminary verdict: both runtime change and kernel/image bump may have contributed. Evidence: canary revert reduced errors quickly; kernel rollback reduced retransmits and further lowered errors. Seems like an interaction under concurrency.
Alice Chen: customer impact: partial degradations for a subset of tenants in us-west-2 between 14:00-14:20, retries may have latched. Suggested customer comms: acknowledge degraded performance, note transient underlying infra/runtime change, ETA for full RCA within 48h.
Lucas Nguyen: next steps:
- Stabilize: keep runtime rollback until thorough root cause testing (Owner: Emma, hold until postmortem)
- Image audit: freeze image refresh in us-west-2 until kernel verification (Owner: Maya)
- Telemetry: add KV fetch latency histograms and per-shard queue depth metrics (Owner: Jason)
- Run concurrency reproduce with KV+kernel 6.2.1 combo in staging (Owner: Lucas)
Emma Rodriguez: I'm leaving detailed timeline + hypothesis notes here, handing off to Maya for follow-up. Oncall handoff at 14:25 UTC.
Maya Patel: taking post-incident ownership for RCA. Will schedule follow-up triage in 1h and assign action items.
Bob Singh: collected all logs and uploaded to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1763126400/model-12-logs.tar.gz
Incident Bot: Incident acknowledged resolved (service error rate back within SLOs). Resolution window: 14:20 — 14:22 UTC.
Emma Rodriguez: thanks team. I'll keep the runtime rollback in place and coordinate a controlled deploy once tests are green.
Alice Chen: noted for customer comms, will draft a short blurb for support + status page.
Jason Li: will open a follow-up PR to add defensive timeouts into KV path and a canary matrix to combine kernel versions in staging.
Maya Patel: scheduling RCA doc and assigning owners. Thanks, handing off. :slightly_smiling_face:
Alice Chen: closing thread once postmortem link is posted.
